In 大司農陳臧錢經用, 陳 is the verb 'to report,' not a surname. The clause says that current expenditure had consumed the stored money, not that the official merely presented money for use.

級十七萬 states a price of 170,000 cash per successive grade, not seventeen grades. The revision supplies the monetary unit and preserves the source's puzzling aggregate rather than silently reconciling it.
Its 17 levels were priced in total at over three hundred thousand jin of gold.
Each successive grade cost 170,000 cash; altogether the ranks were worth more than 300,000 jin of gold.
The same 級十七萬 means 170,000 cash per successive grade. Reading it as seventeen levels is wrong, while the source's own aggregate should be retained as transmitted.

Consequently most merchant households above middling means were ruined; the people took to rich food and fine clothes and no longer pursued storing wealth through farming, while because of revenues from salt, iron, and the min-money policy, government expenditures were somewhat easier to meet.

Consequently most merchant households above middling means were ruined; the people took to rich food and fine clothes and no longer pursued storing wealth through farming, while revenues from the salt and iron monopolies and the tax on declared merchant capital gave the government somewhat more room to meet its expenses.
The received term 緡錢 denotes the property tax assessed on merchants' declared capital. 'Declaration-money levy' is opaque English; this wording identifies the fiscal measure plainly.

From the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu, when the Three Offices first cast wuzhu coins, to the middle of the Yuanshi era under Emperor Ping, more than 280 billion coins were cast, it is said.

平帝元始中 means during the middle of the Yuanshi era, and 二百八十億萬餘 is conventionally reported as more than 280 billion coins. The proposal fixed the era phrase but retained the translation's tenfold numerical error.

及莽未誅 means even before Wang Mang was killed. The revision restores 四夷 and 戶口 while giving the accumulated causes and temporal clause natural English syntax.

The Chinese dates the easing to 孝惠、高后時, gives 天下初定 as the motive, and states an absolute ban 市井子孫亦不得宦為吏, not an anonymous 'later' summary with 'largely'.
